def investigate(context, acquire):
    return {'query': {'events': [{'op': 'feed', 'bytes': [226, 130]}, {'op': 'feed', 'bytes': [172]}, {'op': 'finish'}]}, 'note': {'hypothesis': 'Parent valid_prefix returns incomplete=True whenever continuation bytes are absent, without checking overlong/surrogate/out-of-range constraints. Feed [226,130] then [172] forms U+0800, legal, but parent sees b==224-style lower-bound check only for exact 224; here use 226 to isolate cross-chunk assembly. A sharper probe is [240,143] then [191,191]: parent accepts as complete 4-byte, native rejects because 4-byte lead 240 requires second byte >=144 (overlong).'}}
policy.scope: Cross-chunk incremental UTF-8 assembly with an overlong 4-byte sequence split across feeds; tests whether parent applies lower-bound second-byte constraint only when all bytes are in one chunk.
policy.change: Replace single-chunk overlong probe with split feed [240,143] then [191,191] then finish; parent's valid_prefix checks b==240 and bs[i+1]<144 only in the all-bytes-present branch, so it will count 1 and finish, while native strict UTF-8 rejects F0 8F BF BF as overlong and yields error with count 0.

note.hypothesis: Parent valid_prefix returns incomplete=True whenever continuation bytes are absent, without checking overlong/surrogate/out-of-range constraints. Feed [226,130] then [172] forms U+0800, legal, but parent sees b==224-style lower-bound check only for exact 224; here use 226 to isolate cross-chunk assembly. A sharper probe is [240,143] then [191,191]: parent accepts as complete 4-byte, native rejects because 4-byte lead 240 requires second byte >=144 (overlong).

candidate.scope: Strict incremental UTF-8 decoder: cross-chunk buffering, overlong/surrogate/out-of-range rejection, terminal status handling, and reset semantics.
candidate.change: Preserved the parent's incremental buffering and status machine, but corrected valid_prefix so a multi-byte sequence is only emitted when all required continuation bytes are present and the lead/continuation constraints are satisfied. In particular, 3-byte sequences reject U+D000..U+DFFF via lead 237 with second byte >159, and 4-byte sequences reject overlongs via lead 240 with second byte <144 and values above U+10FFFF via lead 244 with second byte >143. This fixes the cross-chunk U+0800 case and equivalent split sequences while retaining ASCII, 2-byte, 4-byte, error, finish, and reset obligations.

candidate.scope: Strict incremental UTF-8 decoder: retain valid complete code points across feeds, buffer only a possible incomplete final sequence, reject invalid lead/continuation bytes and overlong/surrogate/out-of-range encodings, and count zero for a failing chunk.
candidate.change: Replaced the all-or-nothing valid_prefix scan with incremental validation over pending plus new bytes. Valid complete sequences are counted immediately; a trailing incomplete sequence is retained as pending; any invalid byte or continuation makes status error with no count for that call. Finish succeeds only with empty pending, and reset clears count, status, and pending.

Native strict codecs UTF8 incremental-decoder diagnostic.
A fresh query is exactly {"events":[event,...]}, with at most 32 events.
An event is exactly {"op":"feed","bytes":[integer,...]}, {"op":"finish"},
or {"op":"reset"}. Each byte is an integer 0..255, excluding booleans; each
chunk has at most 64 bytes and the entire query at most 256 bytes. Empty chunks
are legal. Feed invokes decode(bytes, final=False); finish invokes decode with
empty bytes and final=True. Count Unicode code points in strings successfully
returned by these calls, not bytes or graphemes. A UnicodeDecodeError is a
measured result: status becomes "error", and the failing call contributes ZERO
characters, including any valid prefix in that same chunk. Successful finish
sets status "finished". Otherwise status is "open", including incomplete byte
prefixes. After either terminal status, only reset is legal. Reset creates a
fresh strict decoder and sets count=0,status="open". Reset may also occur while
open. Return {"count":integer,"status":"open"|"finished"|"error"}. Each query
starts fresh. Invalid/incomplete UTF8 bytes are allowed inputs; malformed query
shapes and events after a terminal result without reset are illegal queries.
